solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Service shown by prince having deadly consequences

parts.note: in tennis a let is a service that clips the net and is replayed
Hal is Prince Hal, the young Henry V in Shakespeare

explanation.surface: A royal's serve on court turns out to be fatal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lethal causes death, so it has fatal results.

clue.text: Advocate opposed to the euro?

definitions.meaning: to advocate a theory is to put it forward for consideration
read whimsically, someone against the euro is in favour of sterling, the British currency

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into PRO (in favour of) and POUND, Britain's currency, the choice of anyone who would rather not adopt the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: To propound an idea is to put it forward, to advocate it for others to consider.

clue.text: What storyteller in square might give, maintaining a favourable image?

definitions.text: What storyteller in square might give
definitions.meaning: a storyteller in a town square gives tellings of tales in front of everyone
the business of keeping an organisation's reputation polished

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading takes the phrase literally: relations are stories told, and a square is a public place.
explanation.definitionFit: Public relations is the professional work of managing how an organisation is perceived.

clue.text: Fashionable singer's trademark producing request for payment

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
a singer is known above all for a distinctive voice

explanation.surface: A trendy vocalist's signature sound earns a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: An invoice is a bill sent to a customer asking to be paid.

clue.text: Bear a single time right sort of money to observe proper behaviour?

parts.note: to bear something is to stand it, to tolerate it
once means on one occasion

indicators.note: sort here is read as a verb, to arrange, so the following word is rearranged

explanation.surface: Putting up with one helping of the correct currency is how to behave properly.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand on ceremony is to insist on formality and correct etiquette.

clue.text: Stiff group of students supported by a lecturer

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the pieces that hold it up

parts.note: a form is a school class

explanation.surface: A rigid class leans on a single academic.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal means stiff and ceremonious in manner, the opposite of relaxed.

clue.text: Excel hiding foot, revealing bit of leg

indicators.note: the foot of a word is its last letter, here kept out of sight

parts.note: to shine at something is to excel at it

explanation.surface: Some spreadsheet conceals a foot and exposes part of a leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding foot' drops the final E of SHINE.
explanation.definitionFit: The shin is the front part of the lower leg.

clue.text: Eccentric taking day off for river feature

indicators.note: taking ... off says a part is removed from the word
completes taking ... off, the removal of a part

parts.note: weird means odd or eccentric

explanation.surface: An oddball takes a day's leave to visit a riverside attraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A weir is a low dam across a river, a feature of many waterways.

clue.text: Reportedly, make outlet for tea?

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word as heard rather than as written

parts.note: to make money is to earn it

explanation.surface: Rumour has it a tea shop is being opened.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea urn is a large vessel with a tap from which tea is dispensed.

clue.text: Prize in harbour recalled happily after vacation

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, turning the word round

parts.note: a port is a harbour

indicators.note: vacating a word empties it of its middle, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: A trophy won in the harbour is fondly remembered after the holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' reads the harbour word backwards, giving TROP; 'after vacation' empties 'happily' of its middle. 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A trophy is a cup or other award given as a prize.

clue.text: Companion with primate by Latin place of worship

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order
an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A friend and a monkey stand beside a Latin speaker in church.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapel is a small church or a room set aside for worship.

clue.text: Mention awkwardly close to pharmacist lotion

indicators.note: awkwardly suggests the letters are clumsily put together, in a new order
the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Bringing up the subject clumsily with the chemist, one asks for a cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkwardly' rearranges MENTION into OINTMEN; 'close to' adds T.
explanation.definitionFit: An ointment is a soothing preparation rubbed on the skin, much like a lotion.

clue.text: Noisy bird restrained by family before start of drinks? There's wishful thinking

indicators.note: being restrained by something means being held inside it

parts.note: a clan is a family group
loud means noisy
the cuckoo is a bird

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A rowdy bird held in by relatives before drinks begin is just a pipe dream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restrained by' sets the noisy bird inside the family; 'start of' supplies the D that follows. The hyphenated phrase comes from Aristophanes' comedy The Birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloud-cuckoo-land is an imaginary realm of fanciful hopes, a byword for unrealistic optimism.

clue.text: Short rest in card game

definitions.meaning: a brief sleep during the day
a card game, short for Napoleon, in which players bid tricks

explanation.definitionFit: Nap means a doze, and is also a card game.

clue.text: Authority in school prepared listening device

parts.note: the head is the headteacher, the person in charge of a school
set means ready or prepared

explanation.surface: The principal, all ready, puts on earphones.
explanation.definitionFit: A headset is a pair of headphones, often with a microphone, for listening.

clue.text: Self-confidence retained by agile goalkeepers

indicators.note: retained by means kept inside, so the letters lie within the words

explanation.surface: Nimble keepers are brimming with self-belief.
explanation.definitionFit: Ego is a person's sense of self-importance or self-esteem.

clue.text: Disjointed fight with outsiders in party

parts.note: a scrap is a fight

indicators.note: the outsiders of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A brawl breaks out at the edges of a party that has lost all order.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrappy means fragmented and disorganised, lacking coherence.

clue.text: Like a blue part of floor (not half) in refurbished chalet

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
refurbished means done up and so reordered
not half removes half of the word

parts.note: a tile is one part of a floor

explanation.surface: Like a sad person, half a floor tile sits in a done-up mountain hut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refurbished' gives ATHLEC; 'not half' halves the tile to two letters, set in before the C. A blue is an Oxford or Cambridge sportsperson, so 'Like a blue' means sporty, not sad.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue at Oxford or Cambridge represents the university in sport, so is athletic.

clue.text: One on board facing sign of shame? Avoid expressing an opinion

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor, someone on board ship
a stain on one's character is a mark of disgrace

explanation.surface: A sailor facing disgrace keeps their views to themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to decline to vote or take a side.

clue.text: A ballet or rally arranged to include hot musical venue

indicators.note: to include means to take something inside
arranged means put in a new order

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A dance show or a political gathering is staged to feature something hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' shuffles fourteen letters; 'to include' slips H among them. The Royal Albert Hall is a famous London concert hall, home of the Proms.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Albert Hall is a London concert hall, home of the Proms.

clue.text: Record account in group that's aiming to recover animal

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: AA, Alcoholics Anonymous, is a group whose members are recovering
an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A recovery group keeps a record of accounts concerning a beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The alpaca is a South American animal related to the llama.

clue.text: Idle lines penned during game in retreat

indicators.note: penned means shut in, so the letters go within the other piece
in retreat means going backwards

parts.note: pool is a game played on a table with cues and balls
L is an abbreviation for line, so LL is lines

explanation.surface: Lazy verses are written during a game that is going badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retreat' turns the game backwards to LOOP; 'penned during' sets the two lines between its O's. 'Idle' is a verb here, to laze about.
explanation.definitionFit: To lollop is to lounge or move about lazily, so to idle.

clue.text: Describe clearly at home petty officer consumed by drink

indicators.note: consumed by suggests swallowed, so held inside

parts.note: a pint is a drink, typically of beer
in means at home

explanation.surface: A naval officer, home and swallowed by his pint, explains things plainly.
explanation.definitionFit: To pinpoint something is to identify or describe it precisely.

clue.text: Pair feature in news bulletin

definitions.meaning: a couple in a romantic relationship
a single story or piece in a broadcast or paper

explanation.definitionFit: An item is a couple who are dating, and also a single news story.

clue.text: Cloth not new put round English breakfast dish

indicators.note: put round means placed around another piece
not means without, so the following letter is dropped

parts.note: muslin is a light cotton cloth

explanation.surface: Fabric wrapped round an English breakfast dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes N from MUSLIN, giving MUSLI; 'put round' wraps it round E.
explanation.definitionFit: Muesli is a breakfast cereal of oats, nuts and dried fruit.

clue.text: Light opening to exhibition held by artist

indicators.note: held by means contained inside

parts.note: Francis Bacon was a British painter

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A painter clutches the start of a show and sheds some light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening to' gives E; 'held by' puts it inside BACON.
explanation.definitionFit: A beacon is a signal light or fire set up as a warning or guide.

clue.text: Scandinavian leaving fine hostel

indicators.note: leaving says the letter goes out of the word

parts.note: a Finn, from Finland, is loosely a Scandinavian
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A Nordic traveller checks out of a good lodging.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn is a hostelry offering food and lodging.

clue.text: Revered figure and kind soul? The odds are non-existent

indicators.note: odd-numbered letters are taken away, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A worshipped figure and a gentle spirit have no chance.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the odd letters of 'kind soul' leaves I, D, O, L.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is an object or person of worship or adoration.
